title: OpenAI ChatCompletions -> Redwood v2: translation adapter and streaming fidelity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a robust translation adapter that maps legacy OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response shapes into Redwood v2 canonical API objects and back. The adapter must preserve semantics for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output features so existing customers using OpenAI-style SDKs can switch to Redwood endpoints with minimal client-side changes. This ticket covers the server-side mapping layer + small compatibility shim used by the hosted API gateway.
acceptance_criteria: Requests using the OpenAI ChatCompletions request shape (messages array, model, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stream, function_call, n, stop) are correctly translated into Redwood v2 message batches and runtime options without loss of intent.

Streaming mode (stream=true) produces delta events with token diffs that can be mapped to OpenAI-style 'choices' with incremental 'delta' fragments; function call arguments streamed across multiple deltas are concatenated and emitted as a final function call in the non-streaming completion object.

Function/tool calling semantics: when OpenAI function_call is present, the adapter routes tool calls to Redwood tool invocation hooks and maps tool responses back into the OpenAI choices[].message.function_call content, preserving name and arguments formatting.

Structured outputs (json_schema / zod-like validators sent via system prompt) are surfaced as Redwood structured responses and converted into content following the OpenAI shaped 'content' field; schema validation failures result in a predictable error type mapped to OpenAI error model.
Edge cases: partial tokens, role/name differences, assistant -> function messages, and stop-sequence behavior are reconciled and tested across the top 10 customer prompts.
Integration tests in CI verify parity for 50 canonical prompt samples comparing Redwood-adapter outputs to legacy OpenAI gateway outputs within tolerances for tokenization and streaming order.
technical_notes: Map 'messages' roles directly; preserve 'name' if provided, fallback to role for Redwood message envelope.
Translate sampling params: temperature -> temperature, top_p -> top_p, but clamp/normalize to runtime supported ranges and document differences.

Implement a streaming buffer that emits OpenAI-style 'data: {"id":..., "choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}]}

' lines; preserve 'finish_reason' semantics for function_call vs stop vs length.

Function call streaming: stream name on first function call delta, stream args across following deltas. After final 'finish_reason': 'function_call', emit full choices object with message.function_call.arguments as concatenated string and a parsed JSON field if arguments are parseable.
Error mapping: Redwood runtime errors (capacity, timeout, model-mismatch) should be translated into OpenAI-compatible error codes and messages; include suggestion field where applicable.
Latency: adapter must add <=2ms median overhead for non-streaming requests and <=5ms overhead for streaming when running in same container as runtime process.
design_decisions: Keep adapter stateless: do not store intermediate streaming chunks across requests beyond connection lifetime; use in-memory stream aggregation for function args while streaming a single response.
Prefer explicit transformation functions with small, well-tested mapping units (request -> canonical -> runtime) instead of ad-hoc string rewrites to reduce future bugs when adding new features.
When semantic differences exist (e.g., stop-sequence handling), prefer behavior that preserves customer intent over strict wire-format parity; document these choices in the compatibility guide.
Expose an opt-in 'strict_openai_compat' flag for customers who want byte-for-byte event format parity for legacy clients.
risk_mitigation: Add e2e regression tests covering common function call streaming patterns to catch broken concatenation ordering.
Throttle and circuit-breaker mapping to avoid cascading errors when Redwood runtime rejects tool invocations.
Run closed beta with a small set of high-usage customers to validate real-world streaming behavior before wide rollout.
Add telemetry events that annotate translated requests so we can trace customer bug reports back to adapter transformations.
qa_plan: Unit tests for every mapping rule (role/name, sampling param normalization, stop sequences).
Property-based tests for streaming token chunk joins to ensure function_call.args are reconstructed correctly from arbitrary chunk boundaries.
Integration tests exercising the hosted gateway that assert byte-stream lines match expected OpenAI pattern for streaming and final non-streaming shapes match canonical OpenAI objects.
Load test: simulate 500 concurrent streaming connections for 10 minutes to validate connection stability and adapter resource usage.
deployment_plan: Feature flag rollout: behind 'openai_compat_adapter' feature flag per-tenant; default off for new tenants.
Canary rollout on Dedicated staging cluster, then 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours with increased tracing.
Monitor for error-rate regressions and 95th percentile tail latency; auto-roll back if thresholds exceeded.
Documentation: add compatibility guide and code snippets for Node/Python showing migration path.
